Out of all ancient Azlant’s clockwork creations, clockwork whales are perhaps the most impressive—or at least the among the largest. Shaped like a bizarre fusion of a shark and an enormous toothed whale, clockwork whales patrolled the shipping lanes around Azlant for centuries before Earthfall shattered the continent, sinking it beneath the waves. Outfitted with complex programming and sensory arrays that allowed for near-perfect navigation, clockwork whales are thought to have been used primarily for securing new and safe nautical routes, although some served as naval transports during Azlant’s cold war with the empire’s ancient enemy, the alghollthus.

With jaws nearly a third of its entire length, a clockwork whale’s bite can slice neatly through smaller seafaring vessels and inflict devastating damage to the hulls of larger ones. Clockwork Whale Out of all ancient Azlant’s clockwork creations, clockwork whales are perhaps the most impressive—or at least the among the largest. Shaped like a bizarre fusion of a shark and an enormous toothed whale, clockwork whales patrolled the shipping lanes around Azlant for centuries before Earthfall shattered the continent, sinking it beneath the waves. Outfitted with complex programming and sensory arrays that allowed for near-perfect navigation, clockwork whales are thought to have been used primarily for securing new and safe nautical routes, although some served as naval transports during Azlant’s cold war with the empire’s ancient enemy, the alghollthus. With jaws nearly a third of its entire length, a clockwork whale’s bite can slice neatly through smaller seafaring vessels and inflict devastating damage to the hulls of larger ones. These gears swiftly cut those swallowed whole into fragments that are then slowly washed away by the flow of water through tiny gaps in the creature’s body. This behavior has led some scholars to posit that the constructs are created at the behest—or at least with the blessing—of the Lady of Graves. Magrim, the demigod of the dwarven afterlife, is also believed to have some connection to ravenous crypts, as suggested by the fact the pediments of many crypts are carved with the scowling visages of dwarven elders.

When the runelords first created the Emerald Chambers, an order of martial spellcasters was established to protect Xin’s tomb. Known as the Silent Devotees, members of this order cut out their own eyes and tongues in a gesture intended both to prove their devotion and to ensure that knowledge of the Emerald Chambers would never spread beyond the order. After an initial surge of volunteers, interest in the order waned once the duplicitous nature of the runelords (and rumors of their involvement in Xin’s assassination) came to light. Today, only a few dozen silent devotees remain.

The devotees expanded the scope of their mission after the runelords claimed portions of the Emerald Chambers for their personal use. These devotees fitted their empty eye sockets with emeralds magically imbued with the site plans for the Chambers, allowing them to patrol the extradimensional space in its entirety. Combined with the raw magic flowing through the Chambers, the emeralds turned the skin of the devotees a pallid green but also gifted them with a sort of immortality, such that the remaining devotees seem immune to the ravages of time. Today, the Silent Devotees are something more than the humans they once were. **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Silent Devotee](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4916) **Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 90 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Thassilonian](/Languages.aspx?ID=52), [Varisian](/Languages.aspx?ID=174); telepathy 100 feet **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +28, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +26, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +25, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +28 **Str** +5 **Dex** +8 **Con** +5 **Int** +6 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +3 **Untouched by Time** Though not undead, silent devotees don’t age as most mortal creatures do. They don’t eat, drink, sleep, or breathe. **Items** _[+2 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [wounding longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_ --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +28 **Will** +25 +2 status to all saves vs. auditory **HP** 255 **Immunities** [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=634) poisons, [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** sonic 15 **Pall of Silence** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629)) 10 feet. The silent devotee is surrounded by an aura that suppresses sound, granting the silent devotee resistance to sonic energy and a bonus to all saves against auditory effects. Creatures within the aura can’t use sonic attacks, use auditory actions, or Cast a Spell without the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait.
**[Reactive Strike](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=48)** --- **Speed** 30 feet **Melee** longsword +29 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=724)), **Damage** 2d8+13 slashing plus 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 34 - **Constant (7th)** [Truesight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Cruel [Sneak Attack](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=34)** A silent devotee’s Strikes deal and additional 2d6 precision damage to creatures that are [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) or are taking [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86). **Quieting Rune** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) The silent devotee marks a creature within 60 feet they can see with a rune of magical silence. The creature must succeed at a DC 34 Will saving throw or be affected as if by a 7th-rank _silence_ spell. The rune lasts for 1 minute or until the devotee dies. A creature can be marked with only one Quieting Rune at a time. If the devotee uses this ability again, any previous Quieting Rune they’ve created ends. **Transdimensional Step** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) The silent devotee teleports to an unoccupied space within 30 feet.
Xin-Undoros The most devoted member of the Silent Devotees was surely Xin-Undoros, a loyal champion of Xin and one of the order’s first volunteers. Though he predicted Earthfall, Xin-Undoros failed to warn the runelords of the catastrophe, blaming them for the death of his beloved emperor. As punishment for this treachery, Xin-Undoros became a graveknight shortly after the end came. While this transformation returned Xin-Undoros’s ability to speak, he still refuses to do so, regarding such an act as a violation of his eternal oath.

For a person who would one day claim to be the reincarnation of not just one, but two, former runelords, Aethusa's childhood was nothing if not ordinary. Born to a pair of administrators in the ancient Thassilonian nation of Edasseril, Aethusa was by all accounts a bright, obedient, but ultimately unexceptionable child. Though her lack of ambition was a constant source of worry for her parents, everyone assumed she would eventually follow in their footsteps, becoming a loyal soldier in Edasseril's bureaucratic legions.

 Whatever hope Aethusa's family had for her future faded as she entered adolescence. At the age of 12, Aethusa cast aside traditional schooling, delving instead into the study of ancient history, obscure languages, and the rune magic of the runelords. When their daughter's newfound passions proved unshakable, Aethusa's parents suggested she enroll in one of Edasseril's arcane academies, where at least  she could receive a formal education in such matters. Even then Aethusa rebelled, insisting she could learn more—and more quickly—on her own. The conflict came to a head as Aethusa approached her 16th birthday, when she announced her interest in the runelords had been sparked by the conviction that her soul was the reincarnation of the two runelords who shared her name. Arguments that pointed out to her that the original Aethusas lived at the same time didn't sway her convictions and only emboldened her to claim her soul was a merging of both previous lives. Together, Aethusa claimed, the three of them would one day rule not just over a tiny sliver of Thassilon, but the entire nation and beyond.

 Disavowed by her family, Aethusa spent the next few years continuing her studies, mastering magic at a pace that seemed improbable for one who was merely self-taught. Soon, she'd gathered a coterie of followers around her, all of whom believed her claim as the successor of past runelords was neither an empty boast nor vain delusion. Though she showed a talent for rune magic of all kinds, Aethusa selected sloth as her focus, believing it to be the most expedient route to power. It was also during this time that Aethusa adopted the moniker of the Thrice- Born Queen: a nod to the runelords whose souls she shared, but also a declaration of her right to rule. Aethusa's ambitions would have eventually drawn the attention of the runelords themselves had Earthfall not intervened. When the apocalypse struck, Aethusa was in Xin-Edasseril and became trapped outside of time along with the rest of city's inhabitants. In 4718 ar, when the crystal dome around Xin-Edasseril shattered, Aethusa emerged to a world where the dominion of the runelords had been interrupted, but not entirely erased. Wasting no time, she redoubled her efforts, and in a few short years had solidified herself as the leader of a growing movement to unseat both Runelord Belimarius and Queen Sorshen.

 Whether Aethusa's bid for power might have succeeded no longer matters, as several months ago, the voices Aethusa had heard since childhood began to urge her in a new direction. They compelled her to find Runelord Xanderghul's runewell— and more specifically, the Eye of Arrogance, the extradimensional realm to which Xanderghul had retreated during Earthfall. When she arrived there, however, Aethusa realized that the voices in her head were no longer those of the other Aethusas. Rather, they were the whispers of the Ashen Man, an Ancient One intent on returning Xanderghul's soul to the Universe, using Aethusa as his vessel, and now she struggles with the growing realization that it may well have been this mysterious entity manipulating her all along. Her memories of her time spent being possessed by Xanderghul are hazy and dreamlike. 

<title level="2" right="">Campaign Role</title> In Aethusa's body, Xanderghul established a foothold in the Saga Lands, founded the Risen of the Trinity Star, reclaimed the Crypt of Sin, and created not only a small army of risen runelords, but also a brand-new body for himself. Aethusa can share this with the PCs, but at first, she has no reason to trust them. The most important bit of information she should share with the PCs is that she can still feel a link to Xanderghul, and that she knows if he dies or otherwise leaves his body, his soul can instantly take control of her again, over any distance. If the PCs explain what they've been up to and return her dagger and spellbooks, and help her to recover from her conditions, she'll automatically trust them enough to do so, otherwise the PCs will need to work at bringing her initial attitude of unfriendly up to at least friendly.

 Once she trusts the PCs, she can share what she knows with them, but her traumatic experiences (even after she physically recovers) prevent her from wishing to accompany the PCs on their adventures. She'll travel with them, but as soon as she can, she hopes to find somewhere quiet to hide and continue to recover, mentally, from the ordeal. In the short term, her thirst for revenge against Xanderghul and her fear of being possessed by him again outweighs her desire for power—at least until the runelord's plans are foiled. Additional ways in which Aethusa can aid the PCs are covered in Chapter 3 of this adventure, but left to her own devices, she prefers to retreat to a city like Riddleport, Magnimar, or Korvosa and, for the moment, wait and hope.

 Aethusa's stats below present her once she's fully recovered from her ordeals and has reclaimed her dagger and spellbook (both found in area **B18**); until she's got her spellbook back and has a chance to rest and prepare, she has no spells prepared and must rely upon her cantrips.

Together, Aethusa claimed, the three of them would one day rule not just over a tiny sliver of Thassilon, but the entire nation and beyond. Disavowed by her family, Aethusa spent the next few years continuing her studies, mastering magic at a pace that seemed improbable for one who was merely self-taught. Soon, she'd gathered a coterie of followers around her, all of whom believed her claim as the successor of past runelords was neither an empty boast nor vain delusion. Though she showed a talent for rune magic of all kinds, Aethusa selected sloth as her focus, believing it to be the most expedient route to power. It was also during this time that Aethusa adopted the moniker of the Thrice- Born Queen: a nod to the runelords whose souls she shared, but also a declaration of her right to rule. Aethusa's ambitions would have eventually drawn the attention of the runelords themselves had Earthfall not intervened. When the apocalypse struck, Aethusa was in Xin-Edasseril and became trapped outside of time along with the rest of city's inhabitants. In 4718 ar, when the crystal dome around Xin-Edasseril shattered, Aethusa emerged to a world where the dominion of the runelords had been interrupted, but not entirely erased. Wasting no time, she redoubled her efforts, and in a few short years had solidified herself as the leader of a growing movement to unseat both Runelord Belimarius and Queen Sorshen. Whether Aethusa's bid for power might have succeeded no longer matters, as several months ago, the voices Aethusa had heard since childhood began to urge her in a new direction. They compelled her to find Runelord Xanderghul's runewell— and more specifically, the Eye of Arrogance, the extradimensional realm to which Xanderghul had retreated during Earthfall. When she arrived there, however, Aethusa realized that the voices in her head were no longer those of the other Aethusas. Rather, they were the whispers of the Ashen Man, an Ancient One intent on returning Xanderghul's soul to the Universe, using Aethusa as his vessel, and now she struggles with the growing realization that it may well have been this mysterious entity manipulating her all along. Her memories of her time spent being possessed by Xanderghul are hazy and dreamlike. Campaign Role In Aethusa's body, Xanderghul established a foothold in the Saga Lands, founded the Risen of the Trinity Star, reclaimed the Crypt of Sin, and created not only a small army of risen runelords, but also a brand-new body for himself. Aethusa can share this with the PCs, but at first, she has no reason to trust them. The most important bit of information she should share with the PCs is that she can still feel a link to Xanderghul, and that she knows if he dies or otherwise leaves his body, his soul can instantly take control of her again, over any distance. If the PCs explain what they've been up to and return her dagger and spellbooks, and help her to recover from her conditions, she'll automatically trust them enough to do so, otherwise the PCs will need to work at bringing her initial attitude of unfriendly up to at least friendly. Once she trusts the PCs, she can share what she knows with them, but her traumatic experiences (even after she physically recovers) prevent her from wishing to accompany the PCs on their adventures. She'll travel with them, but as soon as she can, she hopes to find somewhere quiet to hide and continue to recover, mentally, from the ordeal. In the short term, her thirst for revenge against Xanderghul and her fear of being possessed by him again outweighs her desire for power—at least until the runelord's plans are foiled. Additional ways in which Aethusa can aid the PCs are covered in Chapter 3 of this adventure, but left to her own devices, she prefers to retreat to a city like Riddleport, Magnimar, or Korvosa and, for the moment, wait and hope.
